title: the manifest promises a detector consumers cannot run, and upgrade has no preview -- one builtin closes both
body:
# 0017: the manifest promises a detector consumers cannot run, and upgrade has no preview -- one builtin closes both

## Tags

vendoring, manifest, upgrade, preview, highlander, doctor

## Summary

Two absences with one shape. First: `manifest.sha256`'s header says an edit to a devbin-owned file is DETECTED -- and doctor detects it against the INSTALL-TIME checksums. What no consumer can ask is the vs-SOURCE question: which vendored files differ from the devbin these bytes came from? That is the question issue 0016's divergence measurement needed (the count named in discussion was three, the truth was four, and two of the four were news to everyone), and the 2026-08-24 upgrade audit needed it again and hand-built fingerprints to get it. Second: `upgrade` has no preview -- its options are `--from` and `--force` only, so "what would this change" is unanswerable short of running it. Both questions are the same comparison, tree-vs-source, which is why one builtin closes both.

## Reproduction

Not a defect reproduction -- an absence, measured by what consumers built to fill it. Two estates have independently written the missing tool: Intent's `int vendor` (states MATCHES / DIVERGED / MISSING / UNLISTED, reports, never restamps) and Laksa's `check vendor` ("vendored from bd2bc4d1 ... level with upstream, nothing to vendor down", observed 2026-08-24). Counting doctor's manifest arm (the vs-install half), the concern now has three homes fleet-wide and none of them is upstream.

## Root Cause

The detector question was answered where the source lives (this repo can diff itself against anything) and never shipped to where the question is asked. Same shape as an unwired git hook: not failing, reporting nothing, and reporting nothing is indistinguishable from the expected state.

## Impact

A consumer carrying local patches -- a SUPPORTED state per the manifest's own header -- cannot enumerate its own divergence. An operator about to run `upgrade` cannot see what it will touch. Both were paid for in real sessions (0016's carry; the 2026-08-24 sweep audit).

## Proposed Fix

A `devbin vendor` builtin (or `doctor --vendor`): compare the vendored tree against the recorded source at its recorded `source_commit`, report MATCHES / DIVERGED / MISSING / UNLISTED per file, never restamp the manifest, and exit by the standard codes so it can serve as upgrade's dry-run. Two constraints, both paid-for: its precision is measured FROM A CONSUMER INSTALL, never from this checkout -- D12 runs lib/ in place, so the source tree is clean by position and can validate nothing (intent-vc, 2026-08-24). And any hand-rolled comparison loop must not use `path` as a variable name (0016's zsh trap: `path` is tied to PATH and its destruction reports 27/27 diverged).

## Related

- 0016 -- proposed this as its step 4, "separable from the four patches and not blocking them"; the four patches landed 2026-08-17, this is the remainder
- 0021 -- the upgrade-loop refinements this builtin's preview role touches
- Intent `int vendor`, Laksa `check vendor` -- the two consumer-side implementations to fold in

## Resolutions

**CLOSED 2026-08-24 (vc).** `devbin vendor` ships: `lib/cmd/vendor` as a thin coordinator over `vendor_states` and `source_direction` in `lib/install`, which the module registry already names as THE home for vendoring and manifest work -- so no new module, and the logic sits beside `manifest_check` rather than in a second place that knows how to compare a tree.

**THE ISSUE ASKED FOR TWO BASELINES AND CALLED THEM ONE.** "Compare against the recorded source at its recorded `source_commit`" and "serve as upgrade's dry-run" are different comparisons: the dry-run has to read what upgrade will actually copy, which is the source's WORKING TREE, and the recorded commit is what these bytes came FROM. They coincide only when the source is clean and unmoved. Resolved by comparing against the working tree -- the actionable question, and the one both consumer implementations already answer -- and printing the recorded commit, the source's current state and the direction between them in the header of every run. An instrument green over an unnamed baseline certifies nothing, so the baseline is named before any verdict.

**The states are seven, not four.** `level` / `behind` / `patched` / `converged` / `absent` / `orphaned` / `released`, plus `unlisted` as a note. The extra ones are not embellishment: `behind` and `patched` are the same byte-difference with opposite consequences (upgrade replaces one and refuses the other), and `converged` is the cell that only exists because this is a CROSS PRODUCT of two comparisons rather than either alone --

|              | source equal | source differs | source absent |
| ------------ | ------------ | -------------- | ------------- |
| **ok**       | level        | behind         | orphaned      |
| **modified** | CONVERGED    | patched        | released      |

-- and the capitalised cell is what 0021's first finding was about, which is why one pass closed both.

**Exit status.** 0 when the tree is level with its source, non-zero when it is not; non-zero is an answer rather than a fault, following `doctor`'s precedent that a reporter returns 1 on a negative verdict. That is what lets `upgrade` keep 0 for "I completed" (0021, finding 2). It is deliberately NOT a `check` gate: carrying local patches is a supported state per the manifest's own header, so a gate red on it would assert a verdict this project does not hold -- the argument that keeps `fmt md` out of `check format`.

**Both stated constraints honoured, and checked rather than asserted.** Precision is measured from a consumer INSTALL: every fixture installs through the real installer into a scratch target (D24), and the D12 checkout case has its own test proving `vendor` refuses there and names D12 instead of the dead-end `install --into` remediation. No `path` variable exists anywhere in the comparison loop (0016's zsh trap); the locals are `rel`, `abs` and `src_rel`.

**NOT done, and not claimed:** Intent's `int vendor` and Laksa's `check vendor` are untouched. The upstream detector now exists, so each consumer's node can retire its local one when it chooses -- three homes became four before they become one, and collapsing them is that node's call, not this issue's.

A false-green guard refuses a run that compared zero files. It is unreachable from a valid source, since `is_devbin_source` has already insisted on `bin/devbin` and a `lib/helpers`, and it is documented in the code as unreachable rather than covered by a test that could never go red.
